Onshape UI kit

The frame and every control an app inside Onshape needs, measured 2026-09-11 from a live Part Studio and built once in src/ui/. Nothing on this page was designed; each value came out of tools/style-probe.mjs, tools/chrome-extract.mjs, tools/viewcube-extract.mjs or tools/look-compare.mjs. Add ?theme=light to flip. Building on it: docs/UI_KIT.md.

The frame, live

This is createShell, createToolbar, createPanel and mountViewCube, called the way an app calls them, with the product's rails and tab bar switched on so the whole frame can be compared with a Part Studio. Hover a tool for its tooltip, open the caret on the split tool, right-click the stage, right-drag it to orbit, click the cube, open the dropdown under it.

The toolbar, tool by tool

Every tool in Onshape's toolbar has a label in the DOM and every one is hidden except Sketch: one labelled action, the rest icons with tooltips. A row of text buttons is the clearest sign a panel was built without looking at a Part Studio. The sizes are theirs.

Menus and the tooltip

The two things in the chrome that float, and the two that carry a shadow. The dropdown menu is their camera menu reproduced entry for entry; the compact one is their context menu. Both are the same component with a compact flag.

The panel

The filter row, a section header with its 30px buttons, and 26px rows with a 20px icon box and a 17px glyph. Children indent 19px under a guide line; default geometry is dimmed to 0.5; a custom feature gets an initials chip. Hover is #0a4780, selection is #134e96 — measured from pixels, where the token sheet's --os-row-fill-selected said #094174.

The twelve that matter most

Ordered by how fast a person notices. Each one decides, on its own, whether a panel reads as part of the product.

Colour

The accent is not the same blue in both themes and not a lightened version of one: #3e94ff on dark, #1651b0 on light. Axis colours invert in weight rather than staying put — saturated and dark on white, pale and light on #333.

Type

Onshape uses Flama and really loads it; a guest origin cannot. Measured over eight strings at 14px, system-ui is −0.90% off Flama's metrics while Onshape's own declared fallback lands on Open Sans at +4.39%. Copying their font-family verbatim is nearly the worst available choice. Line-height is 1.5 everywhere.

Controls

No button, input, tab, toolbar, panel, dialog or row carries a box-shadow; only the menu and the tooltip do. A pressed toggle takes the accent, not a darker grey.

Icons

Filled glyphs on a 0 0 20 20 grid, drawn at 20×20 — measured, 82 of 91 symbols on that viewBox and 201 of 201 painted shapes filled, none stroked. The row below puts a filled mark next to the stroked equivalent every popular icon set ships. The difference is the loudest single mismatch available to an embedded panel.

← theirs  ·  every popular set →
the kit's set, drawn to their conventions; names are what the tool does

How it behaves

Colour and type decide whether a panel looks like the product. This decides whether it feels like it. Orbiting on the right button is the one that surprises people, and it is felt on the first drag.

Box select, captured mid-drag — a net exists only while a button is held, is drawn in WebGL, and has no CSS token to read. Direction decides the rule, and the mode is marked by both colour and dash, which survives a glance and survives colour blindness.

left → right — takes what is entirely inside — solid
right → left — takes anything it touches — dashed

A click toggles an entity in the selection; a box select adds what it catches; a click on empty space clears, and so does Space. Running a command does not clear it: the selection is what the tool acts on. Picking a different kind of entity starts a new set.

Geometry highlights amber

This catches people out, because the chrome's accent is the blue #3e94ff, so a viewport that highlights in blue looks self-consistent and still reads as the wrong application. The blue is for interface state; the amber is for geometry.

Manipulators

A white line in a dark casing, so it reads against a lit face, a dark face and the flat background without changing colour. The casing is the whole trick. Hover and drag colours swap between themes rather than lightening.

line, outline, and the same handle on a lit face and on the background

The view cube

Read out of Onshape's own client code, not drawn from a picture of it — it is live in the frame above. Each face is two rounded plates: a 97% plate in the back colour under a 75% plate in the canvas colour, which is the light frame around a dark centre. Each corner is a disc. 14 pick regions: 6 faces, 8 corners, no edges. A face is an axis view; a corner is a trimetric, 30° off the nearer of front and back and 30° up. The arrows turn 15° (shift 90°, ctrl 5°). Right-drag is a turntable about world Z at three turns per canvas diagonal, and the model follows the mouse.

The viewport

Flat #333, zero gradient, and the light follows the camera: the product's own shader is a Phong headlight fixed in eye space, transcribed from its client bundle into PART_GLSL. Ambient 0.5, diffuse 0.5 N·L, a #999 specular at exponent 30, screen-space ambient occlusion at 37.5%, no gamma. Edges are 1px black. The sphere below is drawn with that shader.

Using it

One stylesheet, one import. The shell gives you the hosts; the components fill them; the camera and cube take the stage's corner. docs/UI_KIT.md has the rest.
